definition: A fixed payment amount made by a borrower to a lender at a specified date each calendar month, combining principal and interest.
The ratio of the loan amount to the appraised or purchase value of the underlying collateral asset, expressed as a percentage.
The proportion of a borrower's gross or net monthly income committed to servicing recurring debt obligations.
An underwriting metric used by Indian banks indicating the percentage of a borrower's monthly income absorbed by mandatory fixed debts and rent.
The effective annual cost of credit expressed as a percentage, incorporating interest rate, processing charges, insurance, and statutory fees.
A standardized one-page disclosure document mandated by RBI to be given to borrowers before loan sanction, detailing APR, loan amount, and cooling-off terms.
India's premier credit information bureau that tracks debt repayment track records and calculates credit scores ranging from 300 to 900.
The number of days an installment, principal, or interest payment remains unpaid after its formal payment due date.
An asset classification framework created by RBI to flag early stress in loan accounts before they slip into non-performing status (SMA-0: 1-30 DPD, SMA-1: 31-60 DPD, SMA-2: 61-90 DPD).
A loan advance where interest and/or installment of principal remains overdue for a period exceeding 90 days.

expansion: Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning
definition: RBI's regulatory framework governing when banks can recognize interest income on advances and how much capital must be set aside as loan-loss provisions.
The total monetary value of all loans classified as non-performing by a bank before subtracting impairment provisions.
Gross NPAs minus cumulative loan loss provisions held by the bank, reflecting true unhedged credit risk.
The proportion of gross bad loans for which a bank has set aside capital provisions (Total Provisions / Gross NPAs * 100).

expansion: Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act
definition: An Indian statute enacted in 2002 that empowers banks and financial institutions to auction residential or commercial secured properties to recover NPAs without court intervention.
India's consolidated bankruptcy law enacted in 2016 establishing time-bound resolution for insolvent corporate debtors through the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT).
A specialized financial institution registered under RBI that buys non-performing assets from banks at a discount to resolve or liquidate them.
The maximum working capital loan limit a bank can sanction to a commercial borrower, traditionally assessed using Nayak or Tandon committee formulas.
A measurement of commercial cash flow available to pay recurring debt service obligations: (PAT + Depreciation + Interest on Term Debt) / (Principal Repayment + Interest).
The difference between current assets and current liabilities, representing the long-term capital margin deployed in everyday operations.
RBI mandate requiring domestic commercial banks to allocate at least 40% of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) to designated sectors like agriculture, MSMEs, education, and housing.
The benchmark credit base against which Indian banks calculate mandatory statutory allocations like Priority Sector Lending targets.
A tradable market certificate introduced by RBI that enables banks to achieve priority sector targets by purchasing surplus allocations from other banks without risk transfer.
The ratio of a bank's capital (Tier 1 + Tier 2) to its risk-weighted assets, mandated by Basel III (minimum 9% in India, 15% for HFCs).
The highest-quality loss-absorbing regulatory capital comprising common stock, retained earnings, and statutory reserves.
A bank's assets weighted according to their credit, market, and operational risk profiles to determine statutory capital requirements.
The statutory percentage of Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) that commercial banks must hold in liquid cash with the Reserve Bank of India.
The minimum percentage of deposits that banks must invest in approved securities (such as Central Government G-Secs) or gold.
A low-cost deposit ratio representing the proportion of current and savings account deposits in a bank's total deposit liability base.

expansion: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation
definition: A wholly owned subsidiary of RBI providing statutory deposit insurance coverage up to ₹5 Lakhs per depositor per bank in the event of bank liquidation.
Income tax withheld by banks on interest income earned from fixed and recurring deposits under Section 194A of the Income-tax Act.
A rupee-denominated bank account maintained in India by non-resident Indians (NRIs) where funds and interest are completely tax-free and freely repatriable abroad.
A rupee account maintained by NRIs to manage income earned in India (such as rent, dividends, or pension), subject to Indian income tax and repatriation caps.
A term deposit account opened by NRIs in permitted foreign currencies (USD, GBP, EUR, JPY) that shields the depositor from exchange rate fluctuations.
Mandatory regulatory procedure of identifying and verifying the legal identity and address of customers when establishing a banking relationship.
Statutory rules, regulations, and automated screening procedures designed to prevent criminals from disguising illegally obtained funds as legitimate income.
The six government-authorized identity documents recognized by RBI for KYC: Passport, Driving Licence, Proof of possession of Aadhaar number, Voter ID, NREGA Card, and NPR Letter.
A centralized digital repository managed by CERSAI storing KYC records of financial sector customers, eliminating redundant re-KYC across institutions.
The central national agency responsible for receiving, processing, analyzing, and disseminating information relating to suspect financial transactions to law enforcement.
A mandatory monthly regulatory filing sent to FIU-IND documenting all cash deposits or withdrawals exceeding ₹10 Lakhs or aggregate foreign currency equivalent.
A confidential report that banks must file with FIU-IND within 7 days of identifying transactions with no clear economic rationale or linked to illicit activity.
Individuals who are or have been entrusted with prominent public functions, including heads of state, politicians, and senior judicial/military figures, posing higher AML risks.
An agent of a Regulated Entity who carries out one or more of a lender's functions (customer acquisition, underwriting support, pricing, or recovery) in digital lending.
A credit enhancement structure where a fintech LSP guarantees to compensate a regulated lending partner for credit defaults up to an RBI-mandated cap of 5% of the loan portfolio.

expansion: Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits
definition: The universally recognized set of rules published by the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) governing the issuance and handling of Letters of Credit across international trade.
A financial commitment issued by a bank on behalf of a buyer guaranteeing that payment will be made to an exporter upon presentation of compliant shipping documents.
An irrevocable undertaking issued by a bank to pay a beneficiary a specified sum if the bank's customer defaults on a contractual or financial obligation.
Commercial loans raised by eligible resident Indian entities from non-resident lenders, strictly regulated by RBI under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA).
The single integrated grievance redressal mechanism established by RBI in 2021 covering scheduled commercial banks, NBFCs, and payment system participants.
